title: 1908-1920 Free bridge. Note an Indigenous seasonal encampment on the right
description: This photo of the uncovered Hartland Bridge and the Town of Hartland was taken between 1908 and 1920. To the right, a small structure built by the Polchies family served as their summer retreat. The Polchies family became well-known in the community, often trading or bartering baskets, snowshoes, and fish with local residents. A well-loved story recalls a time when the Chief visited the Polchies' family and fell ill during the visit. Dr. Lorne MacIntosh was called to treat him, and afterwards, presented the Polchies with a bill. “Oh, that’s a lot of money; too much,” he protested. The doctor replied, “It’s not what you do, it’s what you know.” Later that fall, when Dr. MacIntosh needed his snowshoes repaired, he took them to Polchies. When Polchies presented his bill, the doctor exclaimed, “Oh, that’s a lot of money to fix these shoes!” Polchies responded with a smile, “It’s not what you know, it’s what you can do.”
